guide.summary: Private app, one account or team (self-serve, wait none); Public app for many customers' accounts (app review); Public app with response or survey write scopes (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, one account or team (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for many customers' accounts (app review).

composio.note: SurveyMonkey is on Composio's bring-your-own-OAuth-app list, so create the auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio provides no managed OAuth app for SurveyMonkey, so you must register your own app and give Composio its client ID and secret.
reasons: No Composio managed app exists for SurveyMonkey
Production users should see your app name, not Composio's
A dedicated quota instead of one shared across Composio users
Public availability to other accounts requires your own approved public app

prerequisites.title: SurveyMonkey account
prerequisites.detail: You need a SurveyMonkey account to register an app. Competitors of SurveyMonkey may not open a Developer Account.

prerequisites.title: Paid plan with API access for private app users
prerequisites.detail: All users of a private app must be on the same Team and have a paid plan with direct API access.

prerequisites.title: English listing and support
prerequisites.detail: Your first listing must be in English, and your team must provide easily accessible support.

steps.title: Register a draft app
steps.detail: Log in to SurveyMonkey and register an app to get a client ID and secret. Set scopes as required, optional or not required.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and register it in the app settings.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI is saved in the app settings.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Prepare the app listing
steps.detail: Draft honest listing text with scope requirements, an English version, and a compliant app name.

steps.title: Submit the listing
steps.detail: Submit the listing in the Listings tab of My Apps.

steps.title: Request approval for restricted scopes
steps.detail: Contact the help center and describe your app and use case.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.detail: SurveyMonkey reviews the listing. No wait time is documented.
steps.done_when: The app is approved and deployed.

traps.title: For private apps, the API call limit starts at
traps.detail: For private apps, the API call limit starts at 500 calls per day, with contact sales.

traps.title: Draft and Private apps start with limits of 120
traps.detail: Draft and Private apps start with limits of 120 calls per minute and 500 calls per day, with the daily figure given as a starting point and contact sales for changes.

traps.title: Published Public apps in the App Directory can make
traps.detail: Published Public apps in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

traps.title: Draft app is disabled after 90 days
traps.detail: Deploy before the draft period ends or the app is disabled. The help center can extend a disabled app.

traps.title: Private app cannot serve other customers
traps.detail: A private app is limited to one account or Team, and a draft app cannot be authorized by other accounts.

traps.title: SurveyMonkey may reject on unlisted criteria
traps.detail: Approval does not guarantee the app meets the criteria, and rejection can rest on criteria not listed.

traps.title: Terms ban AI training on API data
traps.detail: API content may not be used to train or improve AI or machine learning systems. Check this against your agent's design.

traps.title: Regional datacenters use other API URLs
traps.detail: EU and Canadian accounts use different API base URLs, returned as access_url at token exchange.

traps.title: Refreshing the secret revokes all access
traps.detail: Refreshing the app secret revokes access for all users of the app.

traps.title: Request limits are enforced after repeated overages
traps.detail: Limits are enforced at 100% once an app exceeds them three times in 30 days. Higher limits may cost extra.

blockers.what_it_means: Required scopes must all be approved by the user, and some scopes need a paid plan.
blockers.what_to_do: Set non-essential scopes to optional, and tell customers which scopes need a paid plan.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review the scope settings and mark non-essential scopes optional.

blockers.what_it_means: SurveyMonkey may reject on criteria beyond its checklist.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact the help center and re-check the checklist and the API terms.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the listing against the checklist.

open_questions: How long does listing approval take? Not documented. Ask the SurveyMonkey developer help center.
How long does approval of the two restricted scopes take? Not documented. Ask the help center.
Do customer administrators have to approve the app? Not stated in the terms. Ask the help center.
Does the AI-training ban affect an AI agent that only reads data to produce output? Check the API Developer Terms with SurveyMonkey.
